case_title: Santosh Kumari v. State of J & K & Others
trial_court_outcome: Charges framed against accused for offences punishable under Sections 302, 109, 147, 148, 149 of the Ranbir Penal Code
neutral_facts: The prosecution case was that the husband of the appellant-complainant was assaulted by respondent nos. 3 to 8. The victim was rushed to hospital where he died after 2-3 days. On March 24, 2008, the trial court framed charges against each accused for offences punishable under Sections 302, 109, 147, 148, 149 of the Ranbir Penal Code. The accused were involved in a violent incident where they formed an unlawful assembly with a common object to murder the victim. During the incident, the accused assaulted the victim with the intention to murder him, leading to his death. The trial court framed charges against the accused, and the accused were examined and cross-examined. The High Court initially set aside the trial court's order, but the Supreme Court overturned this decision, finding that the charges were properly framed and the accused were not misled.
